title: C323 — Driver safety belt pretensioner connector
introduction:
This reference identifies the driver safety belt pretensioner connector and maps its cavities to the restraint circuit descriptions. I use the drawing and table together: the cavity label is the address, while the circuit identifier tells you which connection lives there. Similar-looking connector outlines are not enough to settle identity.

Begin with the connector identity table, match each illustrated cavity label to its pin-assignment row, and keep the full front-driver-side qualifier in the Function column attached to that row. The positive and negative markings distinguish the paired circuits; they are not battery or chassis-ground hookup instructions. The pigtail table then provides the separate service-assembly and engineering-shell lookup.

This page teaches identification, not access, connector release, physical terminal-side or wire-side viewing direction, depowering, testing or replacement. Gauge conventions, the Size and Used codes and the terminal-entry shorthand are not decoded here. Their presence does not establish a wire-selection rule or an individual-terminal repair method.

items.name: Qualified personnel and the selected restraint procedure
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Work beyond reading this reference requires the applicable depowering, handling, specified equipment and restoration sequence. This connector sheet is not a standalone service procedure.

items.name: Keep testing within restraint-specific diagnosis
items.detail: Do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test. Record fault information and use the restraint-specific diagnostic path. Connector appearance alone cannot verify correct seating of the connector-position-assurance tab or the resulting shorting arrangement.

edits.why: The circular cavity area is drawn at the right of the elongated housing, with the labels stacked vertically and an inward projection at the circle’s right edge. I use those visible landmarks to read the pictured arrangement. They do not tell the reader how to unlock, disconnect or refit the connector.

Match each drawing label to Cavity and read across for the circuit identifier, color, gauge, full function qualifier and terminal entry. Keeping the complete row together preserves the distinction between the signed restraint circuits. This identifies their documented roles without supplying a test method or proving the pretensioner’s condition.

A pigtail is the connector with attached leads. Match Kit List to Number, then distinguish Service Part from Engineering Shell rather than treating the identifiers as interchangeable. The pigtail and pin-assignment Gauge entries describe separate records; their difference is not permission to choose replacement wire or devise a splice.
